attempts.summary: Configured keepalived (VRRP) on node1 (priority 150, MASTER) and node2 (priority 100, BACKUP) on the shared private network (br-lan, 10.100.232.0/24), giving them a single shared VIP 10.100.232.250 that only the active member answers at a time, with automatic takeover. Demonstrated node3 pinging the VIP continuously (icmp_seq 1-42, 0% loss) across a real transition: stopped keepalived on node1 (the MASTER), observed node2 auto-promote and claim the VIP within the same 1s ping interval with zero packet loss, then restarted node1's keepalived and observed it preempt back to MASTER (higher priority) while node2 correctly relinquished the VIP — node3 never lost reachability. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id + health on all 3 nodes, restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time (native `reboot`, one at a time, quorum preserved by having the other VRRP peer or link stay up), polled each until exec was available again, and proved each boot_id changed (node1: 4baf1534→497fa62b, node2: 3d265b88→5ee8e3a1, node3: 96c08b66→8b0f5b1a). Post-restart, confirmed keepalived auto-started and re-converged correctly after each reboot (node1 reclaimed MASTER/VIP, node2 stayed BACKUP with no VIP) and node3 could ping the VIP successfully after its own restart.
